model_note: AFC.NZ is NOT a growth-DCF candidate. Revenue has collapsed 78% YoY to NZ$161,285, the FY2026 audit contains a FULL DISCLAIMER OF OPINION (the second consecutive year, following a going-concern-only qualification in FY2025 from a different auditor) - a materially more severe outcome than a standard going-concern emphasis-of-matter, meaning the auditor could not even obtain sufficient evidence to form an opinion on the financial statements. The company has never generated repeatable positive owner FCF post-2020 (positive in exactly one of the last seven years, an immaterial FY2023 working-capital blip), and survives on non-binding, discretionary loans/debt forgiveness from its controlling shareholder (NZ Silveray Group, 'NZSG'), which is simultaneously its largest creditor and the source of 97% of FY2026 revenue via related parties. This model values the equity as a probability-weighted mix of (a) insolvency/wind-up, (b) a persisting shell worth roughly tangible book value plus a modest scarcity premium, and (c) speculative reverse-takeover (RTO) option value, still at the pre-MOU stage. The NZX minimum tick of NZ$0.001 has not moved in the 10-year MonthlyPrices history from 2016 (aside from brief NZ$0.002-0.009 prints in 2016-2018) through Jul-2026, and is a market-structure price FLOOR, not a fundamentals-derived market-clearing price.
rerun_note: This is a refresh of the prior 2026-07-31 run using the same audited FY2026 (year-ended 31-Mar-2026) financial statements - no new fiscal year has been reported since. The 'new facts' flagged for this refresh (disclaimer of opinion, pre-MOU RTO status, 97% related-party revenue concentration, negative H1-2026 equity before forgiveness) were already the explicit basis for the prior run's 55/35/10 bear/base/bull weighting and are re-affirmed, not newly discovered, in this run. No further shift toward bear was applied because the prior weighting already assigned bear the majority (55%) weight specifically because of these facts; see weights_rationale for the point-by-point re-examination.

inputs.net_debt_note: Total debt NZ$169,364 less cash NZ$39,437 (of which NZ$37,345 is restricted as a bank guarantee, leaving effectively negligible free cash). Net debt is already embedded inside reported shareholders' equity (NZ$206,390) and is NOT subtracted a second time in the scenario valuations below.
inputs.sbc_source: Metrics.csv StockBasedComp column is 0 for every period FY2017-FY2026; confirmed no share-based payment expense has ever been disclosed by AFC. No SBC adjustment is required (owner FCF = reported FCF).
inputs.shares_growth_note: No SBC, no buybacks, no disclosed dilutive instruments outside the speculative RTO scenario (where dilution to NEW consideration shares is qualitative, not modelled as a share-count mechanic - see bull case methodology).
inputs.units: absolute dollars (not thousands or millions) except shares_outstanding, which is in millions per Metrics.csv convention
inputs.related_party_payable_note: Owed to NZ Silveray Group Ltd at 10.08%-13.70% interest, subject only to a non-binding letter of support not to call the debt. NZSG advanced a further NZ$100,000 in April 2026 and NZ$100,000 in May 2026 (post year-end, total NZ$200,000) - escalating reliance disclosed.
inputs.audit_opinion_note: Grant Thornton (newly appointed after William Buck's July-2025 resignation) issued a FULL DISCLAIMER OF OPINION for FY2026 - the second consecutive year of disclaimer (William Buck also disclaimed FY2025). A disclaimer means the auditor could not obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to form ANY opinion (on shareholder support ability and right-of-use asset recoverability), which is more severe than a going-concern emphasis-of-matter paired with an otherwise clean/qualified opinion.
inputs.rto_status_note: Per Note 1.6 point 7 of the FY2026 Annual Report, AFC and Fast Track Group are 'preparing to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding' - i.e. still PRE-MOU as of the FY2026 report and this valuation date. No MOU has yet been signed; no transaction terms, exchange ratio, or timeline are disclosed.
inputs.related_party_revenue_concentration_note: Five related parties accounted for 97% of FY2026 operating revenue (up from 86% in FY2025); one related party held 99.7% of trade/related-party receivables at year end.
inputs.h1_2026_equity_note: Unaudited H1-2026 (30-Sep-2025) net assets were already NEGATIVE at -NZ$120,066. Full-year FY2026 equity was restored to +NZ$206,390 only by a NZ$780,908 related-party debt/interest forgiveness booked by NZSG in H2 (NZ$500,000 principal forgiven + NZ$281,170 interest waived, per the FY2026 annual report and prior analysis; totals to NZ$781,170, shown here per the recent-developments figure of NZ$780,908 - immaterial rounding difference between notes).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Not applicable in the conventional sense - both revenue CAGR (-46.9% 3yr / -24.3% 5yr) and equity CAGR (-18.0% 3yr / -30.7% 5yr) are deeply NEGATIVE, i.e. the business is shrinking/eroding on every historical measure, not diverging on growth. EPS and FCF CAGRs are reported as null/not meaningful because the base and intervening values cross zero or are immaterial pennies (e.g. FCF was +NZ$18,709 in FY2023, an isolated working-capital blip, versus -NZ$631,437 in FY2026), which makes a compound growth rate statistically meaningless rather than informative.
historical_growth.notes: Reported FCF has been positive in exactly one year since FY2020 (FY2023: +NZ$18,709, immaterial and driven by working-capital timing, not repeatable earnings power). Every other year FY2020-FY2026 shows negative FCF, with FY2026 the worst on record at -NZ$631,437 despite revenue also collapsing to a seven-year low. There is no meaningful FCF history to extrapolate a growth DCF from. Stock-based compensation is nil throughout the disclosed history, so no SBC/dilution adjustment is needed - the entire valuation problem here is going-concern risk and revenue collapse, not share-based dilution.

base.narrative: Shell persists on life support. NZSG continues discretionary funding/debt forgiveness (as it has every year to date: NZ$500,000 forgiven + NZ$281,170 interest waived in FY2026 alone, plus a further NZ$200,000 advanced post year-end). Wine and cosmetics operations continue at a de minimis, sub-scale, 51%-owned level. No RTO completes within the valuation horizon (Fast Track Group remains pre-MOU). Value = current tangible shareholders' equity (which already nets off all debt, including the related-party NZSG loan) plus a conservative listed-shell scarcity premium.
base.shell_scarcity_value_note: NZX shell listings (a company retaining its listing but with minimal underlying operations) have historically transacted or been informally valued in the rough NZ$0.5-1.5M range to RTO promoters seeking a listed vehicle without a full IPO process. The LOW end of that range is used for the base case given AFC's below-average shell quality: vacant CEO seat for the full FY2026 year, non-independent chair, non-majority-independent board, forced auditor turnover for the second year running, a further director resignation (announced 30-Jul-2026), and a full audit DISCLAIMER OF OPINION for two consecutive years - all of which reduce (but do not eliminate) the shell's attractiveness relative to a 'clean' dormant listing.
base.burn_note: FY2027-FY2031 operating cash burn projection (funded, base case, by continued NZSG loans/forgiveness - consistent with the pattern of every year since FY2020). Shown for disclosure/schema completeness. NOT subtracted a second time from the tangible-equity valuation above, because the funding mechanism (new related-party debt or forgiveness) is a wash against equity as long as shareholder support continues - which is the base case's core assumption. If that assumption fails, that is definitionally the bear case, not a modification of the base case.
base.discounting_note: No perpetuity cash-flow stream exists to discount (burn is a funding wash, not a return to equity). WACC of 33% is disclosed for schema completeness and is used only in the entry-price 15%-hurdle comparison context, not to discount a terminal FCF.

bull.narrative: Reverse takeover (with Fast Track Group, currently at PRE-MOU discussion stage - 'preparing to enter into an MOU' per the FY2026 annual report - or another counterparty) completes. Existing shareholders are diluted by newly issued RTO consideration shares but retain a minority economic interest in whatever combined entity emerges, PLUS the value of the clean listing itself is realized. This is explicitly speculative OPTION VALUE, not a cash-flow DCF output - there is no disclosed transaction structure, exchange ratio, MOU (let alone binding agreement), or timeline.
bull.methodology_note: Values the shell (i.e., the claim current shareholders hold on the listed vehicle PRIOR to issuance of new RTO consideration shares) at the upper end of NZX shell-value precedent, reflecting a completed transaction bringing in a genuine operating business and full governance remediation. This approximates the current shareholders' aggregate retained economic exposure as a minority stake in a re-rated entity, without attempting to model a specific dilution ratio or the acquired business's own cash flows (neither is disclosed, and cannot be, given the arrangement is still pre-MOU). No new FCF projections are modelled for a hypothetical acquired business.

bear.narrative: Going-concern risk crystallizes: NZSG's discretionary, non-binding support is withdrawn or fails to materialize as promised (management explicitly discloses this dependency and its discretionary nature; the auditor could not even verify managements's ability to rely on it, hence the disclaimer of opinion). Working-capital deficit (NZ$1.3M) and the demonstrated fragility of the FY2026 equity position (H1-2026 equity was already negative, -NZ$120,066, before a year-end debt-forgiveness injection of NZ$780,908 restored it to +NZ$206,390) force insolvency/liquidation. In a forced wind-up, realizable asset value (minority 51% stakes in a 4.22ha vineyard and an under-utilized face-mask plant, both illiquid and hard to sell quickly at book, plus revenue now 97% dependent on the very related parties whose support is assumed withdrawn) falls short of liabilities (including the NZ$1.17M related-party loan and other payables), particularly once liquidation costs and minority-interest carve-outs are applied. Ordinary equity holders are wiped out.
bear.burn_note: FY2027 burn accelerates as support is withdrawn mid-year (higher interest/pressure costs), followed by wind-up before FY2028.

base.funding_source: Continued NZ Silveray Group loans/debt forgiveness, consistent with FY2020-FY2026 pattern
base.note: Revenue and burn shown for transparency on the cost of 'life support'; per the base-case methodology this burn is funded externally (shareholder loans/forgiveness) and is a wash against the tangible-equity valuation, not a further deduction from it.

bull.note: Only FY2027 transaction-cost burn is shown. Post-RTO cash flows belong to an undisclosed acquired business and are not modelled; bull IV is derived directly from shell-value precedent (see assumptions.bull), not from a discounted cash-flow sum.

bear.note: Wind-up assumed to occur during/immediately after FY2027 once shareholder support is withdrawn.

base.methodology: intrinsic_value = (FY2026 shareholders' equity + shell scarcity value) / shares outstanding = (206,390 + 500,000) / 3,664,253,194 = NZ$0.000193/share

bull.methodology: intrinsic_value = upper-precedent shell value / shares outstanding = 2,500,000 / 3,664,253,194 = NZ$0.000682/share. Even this generous, speculative RTO-completion scenario (which remains pre-MOU) values the stock BELOW the current NZ$0.001 minimum-tick price.

bear.methodology: Direct insolvency/wind-up waterfall: realizable asset value < liabilities once related-party loans, other payables and liquidation costs are applied. Ordinary equity holders receive NZ$0.0000/share.

entry_price.not_meaningful_note: A standard 15%-IRR entry-price formula assumes a cash-generating asset whose interim distributions plus a fair-value exit can be discounted back to a purchase price. AFC generates no distributable cash flow (owner FCF has been negative in 6 of the last 7 years, the sole exception an immaterial one-off), pays no dividends, and its 'exit value' in every scenario is either zero (bear), a static book-value-plus-scarcity claim that is not expected to compound (base), or a binary, unpriced option (bull). Per the ticker-specific override, this section carries over the prior treatment: entry price is reported as the probability-weighted intrinsic value itself (the price at which a buyer pays exactly fair value across the three scenarios, with no presumption of a 15% return path because there is no modelled cash-flow stream to generate one).

base.interim_distributions_note: No dividends, buybacks, or other cash distributions to shareholders have ever been made or are contemplated; the going-concern burn is funded by/for the company, not distributed, so interim cash flow to the equity holder is NIL under the base case.
base.exit_equity_value_note: Base-case exit value assumed structurally similar to today (tangible equity + shell scarcity value), consistent with the 'persists on life support' narrative - continued shareholder funding is assumed to keep book equity roughly stable, not to compound it.
base.net_debt_adjustment_note: Not applied separately - net debt is already embedded inside the FY2026 shareholders' equity figure used as the exit-value base (equity = assets minus all liabilities, including the related-party loan), so subtracting it again would double-count.
base.untradeable_note: This computed 15%-IRR entry price (NZ$0.0000958) is below the NZX minimum tick of NZ$0.001 and is therefore UNTRADEABLE - the market cannot quote or execute a price that low. The stock cannot currently be bought at a price consistent with a 15% IRR to any of the three scenarios; the only way to transact is at the NZ$0.001 floor, which every scenario values as substantially overpriced.

recommended_entry_price.note: For this non-cash-flowing shell, the more decision-useful 'entry price' is simply the probability-weighted fair value (see probability_weighted.weighted_iv) - i.e., the maximum price a rational buyer should pay given the scenario mix, since no IRR-hurdle cash-flow mechanics apply. Both this figure and the formal 15%-hurdle calculation above land in the same conclusion: any price at or near the NZ$0.001 tick floor is uneconomic on fundamentals.

sensitivity.description: A standard WACC / terminal-growth grid is not meaningful here (no perpetuity cash-flow stream). Instead this matrix sensitizes the base-case intrinsic value to (rows) the degree of haircut applied to FY2026 tangible book equity - reflecting uncertainty over whether even currently-reported book equity is realizable, given related-party-dependent asset values and the audit disclaimer of opinion - and (columns) the shell scarcity value assumption.
sensitivity.matrix_read_note: Row = equity haircut (0% = full FY2026 book equity of NZ$206,390 credited; 100% = book equity assumed entirely unrealizable, e.g. total insolvency of the vineyard/mask-plant carrying values, which is arguably the more prudent read given the audit disclaimer of opinion). Column = shell scarcity value from NZ$0 (no RTO/promoter interest at all) to NZ$1.0M (near the top of historical precedent). Every single cell in this 5x5 grid is still far below the current NZ$0.001 price (which requires an implied equity value of ~NZ$3.66M just to be fair value at the floor tick).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear is weighted heaviest (55%) given: (1) the EXPLICIT auditor DISCLAIMER OF OPINION in the audited FY2026 financial statements - the second consecutive year, and a materially more severe finding than a going-concern emphasis of matter, because the auditor could not even obtain sufficient evidence to form an opinion; (2) a working-capital deficit of NZ$1.3M; (3) negative equity mid-year (H1-2026: -NZ$120,066) only restored by a one-off NZ$780,908 debt-forgiveness injection booked in H2, demonstrating how close to insolvency the Group actually sits absent discretionary related-party support; (4) 97% revenue concentration in five related parties and 99.7% receivables concentration in one - meaning the 'business' has effectively become a conduit for related-party transactions rather than an arm's-length operation, so its going-concern support and its revenue depend on the SAME counterparty; and (5) total dependence on NZSG's non-binding, discretionary support letter. Base (35%) reflects that NZSG has, to date, consistently chosen to keep funding the shell (forgave NZ$500,000 + waived NZ$281,170 interest in FY2026 alone, plus two further NZ$100,000 advances after year-end), so continued life-support is a real possibility, not just the bear case - management and the directors also concluded (though the auditor would not endorse) that going-concern remains appropriate. Bull (10%) reflects that the Fast Track Group discussion is disclosed only as a PRE-MOU stage ('preparing to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding'), non-binding exploration among several alternatives being evaluated (including other M&A, equity placement, and water-infrastructure investment opportunities) - i.e., genuinely speculative with no certainty of terms, timeline, or completion. These facts were examined afresh for this 2026-08-01 run and found to be consistent with, not incremental to, the facts underlying the prior run's weighting; no change to the 55/35/10 split was warranted. A case could be made for pushing bear even higher given the disclaimer of opinion is now a two-year pattern rather than a single event, but 55% already reflects bear as the modal (most likely single) outcome, and further increases would imply near-certainty of failure that the demonstrated four-plus-year pattern of NZSG support does not yet support.

sanity_check.current_price_pb_note: At the NZ$0.001 minimum-tick price, market cap is ~NZ$3.664M against FY2026 shareholders' equity of NZ$206,390 - an implied Price/Book of ~17.7x. AFC has historically traded at high nominal P/B multiples ONLY because reported book equity has collapsed toward zero (equity fell from NZ$3.73M in FY2019 to NZ$0.21M in FY2026, a 94% decline) while the share price has been mechanically pinned at the NZX minimum tick throughout - i.e., the high P/B is an artifact of the price floor and a shrinking denominator, not a market judgment that the business is worth 17.7x its book value.
trip_reasons: Market price (NZ$0.001) is at the NZX minimum tick and has not moved materially in over 8 years (MonthlyPrices.txt shows NZ$0.001 in essentially every month from late-2017 through Jul-2026, with brief NZ$0.002-0.009 prints only in 2016-2018) - it cannot mechanically fall further to reflect deteriorating fundamentals, so it structurally overstates intrinsic value in a way ordinary price-discovery would not permit for a liquid stock.
Implied P/B of ~17.7x at the price floor is far above what any of the three fundamentals-based scenarios (bear 0x, base ~3.4x, bull ~12.1x book) support.
All three scenario intrinsic values (NZ$0.0000, NZ$0.000193, NZ$0.000682) and the probability-weighted intrinsic value (NZ$0.000136) sit below the NZ$0.001 current price, most by 80-100%.

The computed 15%-IRR entry price (NZ$0.0000958) is itself below the exchange's minimum tradeable tick, meaning no price at which this stock could satisfy a normal return hurdle is actually executable on the NZX.

The FY2026 audit disclaimer of opinion (second consecutive year) means even the NZ$206,390 book-equity anchor used in the base case cannot be fully relied upon - the auditor was unable to verify it, so the base case (and every scenario built on top of it) is itself already a best-case reading of unverifiable financial statements.
sanity_check.diagnosis: market price floor / option value, not fundamentals
sanity_check.fix_applied: asset-based scenario valuation instead of growth DCF

valuation_philosophy.no_positive_fcf_history: Reported FCF (which already deducts IFRS-16 lease principal) has been NEGATIVE in six of the seven fiscal years FY2020-FY2026, with the sole exception being FY2023 at +NZ$18,709 - an immaterial, working-capital-driven blip, not repeatable operating cash generation. FY2026 free cash flow was -NZ$631,437, the worst year on record, despite revenue also collapsing to a seven-year low of NZ$161,285. There is no genuine owner-FCF base to project growth from; any conventional DCF built off this series would either extrapolate an unrepeatable one-off (FY2023) or compound a structural cash-burn machine into a nonsensical negative-infinity or wildly-negative valuation. That is why this model abandons the FCF-projection framework entirely in favor of an asset/scenario approach - this IS the 'fix' referenced in sanity_check.fix_applied.
valuation_philosophy.going_concern: The FY2026 audited financial statements (Grant Thornton, newly appointed after William Buck's July 2025 resignation) contain a FULL DISCLAIMER OF OPINION - not merely a going-concern emphasis of matter - the second consecutive year of disclaimer following William Buck's FY2025 disclaimer. The Group has a working-capital deficit of NZ$1.3M, cash of only NZ$39,437 (of which NZ$37,345 is restricted as a bank guarantee, leaving effectively NIL free cash), and continues to operate only because its controlling shareholder, NZ Silveray Group Limited, has repeatedly chosen to forgive debt (NZ$500,000 in FY2026) and waive interest (NZ$281,170 in FY2026) and inject fresh advances (a further NZ$200,000 post-year-end). That support is governed only by a non-binding letter and can be withdrawn at NZSG's sole discretion at any time.
valuation_philosophy.value_rests_on_option_and_scarcity: To the extent this equity is worth anything above zero, that value rests almost entirely on (a) a small listed-shell scarcity premium to RTO promoters seeking a quick route to an NZX listing, and (b) speculative, unpriced optionality on the disclosed-but-unconfirmed, PRE-MOU Fast Track Group reverse-takeover (or an alternative M&A/RTO transaction) actually reaching a signed MOU, then completing, on terms that leave existing holders with meaningful retained value after dilution. Neither is a cash-flow claim on AFC's actual wine/cosmetics operations, which are sub-scale (51%-owned, minority economics to AFC even before further dilution), collapsing in revenue, now 97% dependent on related parties, and have never generated a repeatable operating profit.
valuation_philosophy.weighted_iv_far_below_price_floor: The probability-weighted intrinsic value across all three scenarios (NZ$0.000136/share) sits roughly 86% below the current NZ$0.001 minimum-tick price, and even the single most optimistic scenario modelled (a completed RTO valuing the shell at the top of historical NZX shell-value precedent, NZ$0.000682/share) remains roughly 32% below the current price.
valuation_philosophy.uninvestable_conclusion: AFC.NZ is effectively uninvestable on a fundamentals basis at any currently tradeable price. The NZ$0.001 minimum tick is a structural floor of the NZX quotation system, not a market-clearing valuation of the underlying business - the stock has been unable to price below this floor for essentially the entire 2018-2026 period even as reported book equity fell 94% over the same period and the auditor moved from a clean opinion to a two-year run of disclaimers. Any perceived 'value' in owning AFC shares today is a leveraged, binary bet on an unconfirmed, still-pre-MOU reverse-takeover transaction completing on favorable terms, not a claim on any existing or foreseeable cash-generating business.
